newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UK seeks higher rice quotas for its territories.
newsitem.headline: UK seeks higher rice quotas for its territories.

text.p: Britain called on Monday for higher quotas to ensure the survival of the rice industry in its Caribbean overseas territories of Montserrat and the Turks and Caicos Islands, which it said were devastated by EU safeguard measures.

The measures, taken by the European Commission on January 8, led to the loss of 170 private-sector jobs in the rice processing industry in Montserrat, David Davis, Minister of State for European affairs, told EU foreign ministers.
Some 40 percent of the 11,000 population have already left the island due to the threat of volcanic eruptions.
Another 85 jobs were lost in the Turks and Caicos Islands, which have a total population of about 12,500 people, following the closure of a rice factory.
A British official said that Britain hoped for a favourable Commission reaction next week.

The Commission, in response to Italian and Spanish complaints of a sharp rise in rice imports, set the first (January/April) tranche of an annual tariff free quota limiting rice imports from overseas countries and territories (OCTs) at 42,650 tonnes.
OCTs, which are not part of the EU but have strong links with it, were given a special tariff free concession in 1991.
Total imports from OCTs rose from 58,000 to 365,029 tonnes between 1992 and 1996.
